answer: The evidence partially supports a higher straight-red-card probability for dark-skinned than light-skinned players: 28 of 93 estimable specifications were significantly positive, compared with 2 significantly negative, and the median standardized estimate was 0.0286. However, 63 of 93 estimates were indeterminate, 163 of 256 universes were unavailable, and inference changed in 41.9% of exposure-handling comparisons, so the broad hypothesis is not robustly established.
rationale: Positive, statistically supported effects are more common than statistically supported negative effects, but a substantial share of estimable specifications is non-significant or indeterminate and key modeling decisions produce frequent inference changes. The evidence therefore supports the direction in some specifications without demonstrating consistent support for the full hypothesis.
key_evidence: Among 93 estimates with confidence intervals, 28 were significantly positive and 2 were significantly negative.
The standardized effect median was 0.0286, with a 25th–75th percentile range of 0.0118 to 0.0439; the minimum was -0.0258.
Sixty-three of 93 estimates were indeterminate, and 163 of 256 universes were unavailable.
Inference flipped in 41.9% of games-exposure comparisons and 41.7% of straight-red-only versus any-sending-off comparisons.
refinement_reason: The multiverse combines substantively distinct claims about the outcome definition, games-exposure handling, and operationalization of skin tone. These choices materially affect effect estimates or inference, so the broad claim should be separated into narrower claims.
suggested_hypotheses: Among player–referee dyads, dark-skinned players have a higher probability of at least one straight red card than light-skinned players when straight reds are used exclusively and games exposure is handled by a prespecified method.
Among player–referee dyads, the dark-versus-light skin-tone association with at least one straight red card is positive under each prespecified binary skin-tone threshold.
Among player–referee dyads, the dark-versus-light skin-tone association with at least one straight red card is positive under a prespecified rule for combining the two skin-tone raters.
caveats: The supplied effects are on a standardized scale; they do not directly provide an absolute probability difference or odds ratio.
Non-significance and indeterminate results do not establish that the effect is absent.
The evidence includes missing or unavailable universes, and the supplied summaries do not identify which specific universes generated each significant result.

skin_tone_rater_combination.label: Skin-tone score construction
skin_tone_rater_combination.rationale: How should `rater1` and `rater2` be combined into the player skin-tone score before dichotomization?  [found by: direct]

both_raters_thresholded.label: Require both raters to classify as dark
both_raters_thresholded.description: Retain the two separate scores for dichotomization; a player is dark only if both `rater1` and `rater2` meet the selected dark-skin threshold, and light otherwise.

skin_tone_threshold.label: Binary skin-tone threshold
skin_tone_threshold.rationale: Which prespecified threshold should convert the combined skin-tone score into dark versus light skin?  [found by: direct]

at_least_050.label: Dark if score ≥ 0.50
at_least_050.description: Set dark_skin = 1 when the score constructed from the selected rater rule is at least 0.50; otherwise set dark_skin = 0.

at_least_075.label: Dark if score ≥ 0.75
at_least_075.description: Set dark_skin = 1 when the score constructed from the selected rater rule is at least 0.75; otherwise set dark_skin = 0.

above_050.label: Dark if score > 0.50
above_050.description: Set dark_skin = 1 when the score constructed from the selected rater rule is strictly greater than 0.50; otherwise set dark_skin = 0.

red_card_outcome_definition.label: Any-event outcome definition
red_card_outcome_definition.rationale: Should the dyad outcome count only straight red cards, or also second-yellow sendings-off?  [found by: direct]

straight_red_only.label: At least one straight red card
straight_red_only.description: Set outcome = 1 when `redCards` ≥ 1 and outcome = 0 when `redCards` = 0; ignore `yellowReds`.

any_sending_off.label: At least one sending-off of either type
any_sending_off.description: Set outcome = 1 when `redCards` + `yellowReds` ≥ 1 and outcome = 0 otherwise.

games_exposure_handling.label: Handling variation in games per dyad
games_exposure_handling.rationale: How should the `games` exposure difference across player–referee dyads enter the logistic analysis?  [found by: direct]

unweighted_dyads.label: Unweighted dyad-level logistic regression
unweighted_dyads.description: Fit the binary logistic model with one equal-weight observation per row, without using `games` as a weight, offset, or predictor.

games_frequency_weight.label: Weight dyads by games
games_frequency_weight.description: Fit the binary logistic model using `games` as a frequency or analytic weight, so a dyad with 20 games contributes 20 times as much as a dyad with 1 game.

adjust_for_log_games.label: Adjust for log games
adjust_for_log_games.description: Fit the binary logistic model with `log(games)` included as a continuous covariate; do not use `games` as a frequency weight.

covariate_adjustment.label: Adjustment set for the skin-tone association
covariate_adjustment.rationale: Which variables, if any, should be included alongside the binary skin-tone predictor in the dyad-level logistic model?  [found by: direct]

skin_tone_only.label: Unadjusted skin-tone model
skin_tone_only.description: Use only the binary skin-tone indicator as a predictor of the selected dyad outcome, with an intercept.

player_and_league_covariates.label: Adjust for player and league characteristics
player_and_league_covariates.description: Include binary skin tone plus `leagueCountry`, `position`, `height`, and `weight` as predictors; do not include referee-country variables.

player_league_referee_country_covariates.label: Also adjust for referee-country characteristics
player_league_referee_country_covariates.description: Include binary skin tone, `leagueCountry`, `position`, `height`, `weight`, `refCountry`, `meanIAT`, and `meanExp` as predictors. Treat `refCountry` as categorical and the two bias measures as continuous.

dependence_inference.label: Inference for repeated players and referees
dependence_inference.rationale: How should uncertainty account for the fact that rows repeatedly involve the same `playerShort` and `refNum`?  [found by: direct]

model_based_iid.label: Model-based iid standard errors
model_based_iid.description: Use the ordinary logistic-regression covariance matrix, treating the 146028 rows as independent for standard-error and confidence-interval calculation.

player_clustered.label: Cluster by player
player_clustered.description: Use a sandwich covariance estimator clustered on `playerShort`, allowing arbitrary dependence among dyads involving the same player.

two_way_clustered.label: Two-way cluster by player and referee
two_way_clustered.description: Use a multiway sandwich covariance estimator with clustering on both `playerShort` and `refNum`, allowing dependence within either repeated-player or repeated-referee groups.

random_intercepts.label: Random intercepts for player and referee
random_intercepts.description: Fit a mixed-effects logistic model with random intercepts for `playerShort` and `refNum`, and report the fixed-effect odds ratio for binary skin tone using model-based mixed-model uncertainty.
